arguments.command:
python -c "
import parse

# Test with fixed results only
r = parse.Result((1, 2, 3), {}, None)
print('Test 1: Fixed results')
print(f'0 in r: {0 in r}')  # True
print(f'1 in r: {1 in r}')  # True
print(f'2 in r: {2 in r}')  # True
print(f'3 in r: {3 in r}')  # False (index out of range)
print(f'-1 in r: {-1 in r}')  # False (we don't allow negative indices for __contains__)
print()

# Test with named results only
r = parse.Result((), {'spam': 'ham', 'eggs': 'bacon'}, None)
print('Test 2: Named results')
print(f\"'spam' in r: {'spam' in r}\")  # True
print(f\"'eggs' in r: {'eggs' in r}\")  # True
print(f\"'cheese' in r: {'cheese' in r}\")  # False
print()

# Test with both
r = parse.Result((1, 2), {'name': 'world'}, None)
print('Test 3: Mixed results')
print(f'0 in r: {0 in r}')  # True
print(f'1 in r: {1 in r}')  # True
print(f\"'name' in r: {'name' in r}\")  # True
print(f\"'missing' in r: {'missing' in r}\")  # False
print()

# Test through actual parse
r = parse.parse('hello {name}', 'hello world')
print('Test 4: Actual parse result')
print(f\"'name' in r: {'name' in r}\")  # True
print(f\"'missing' in r: {'missing' in r}\")  # False
"
